evidence.note: Claim: git merge dies transiently with 'Could not read from .git/MERGE_MSG' when a concurrent process is mid-merge, and retrying the identical merge (like 'fatal: stash failed') clears it. Refuting observation: the error with MERGE_HEAD already set must NOT be retried. Probe: uv run pytest tests/test_merge_stash_retry.py::test_a_merge_msg_read_error_is_retried — FAILED before the fix (merge returned the raw error), PASSED after (retried, merged).

Implemented in the worktree: ddflow/infra/worktree/_mergecore.py (added _merge_msg_missing + _transient, broadened _merge_retrying_stash retry) and tests/test_merge_stash_retry.py (regression test). Both within declared globs.
uv run ruff check ddflow/infra/worktree/_mergecore.py tests/test_merge_stash_retry.py: All checks passed; ruff format --check: 2 files already formatted.

Hunted vacuous-truth (predicate short-circuits on empty stdout/indented lines), off-by-one (tries<STASH_RETRIES, STASH_RETRY_PAUSE_S*2**n), and retried-but-not-actually-merged; the MERGE_HEAD guard mirrors _stash_failed so a merge already begun is never retried. Regression test ships in the same commit.

Did not re-implement: reused the existing _stash_failed/_overwritten predicate pattern in _mergecore.py; no new backoff/extraction needed (first drift of the retry predicate, library reuse still the default).
